name: INS Sanshodhak

header.one_liner: Indian Navy hydrographic survey vessel; lead ship of the GRSE I-class survey ship series (four ships); supports seabed/charting survey for submarines and navigation.
header.indigenous_label: Broadly indigenous hull; survey systems partly sourced

what_it_is.prose: INS Sanshodhak is the lead ship of the Indian Navy's I-class (P-82) hydrographic survey vessel series, built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) in Kolkata. The four-ship class (Sanshodhak, Sanshodhan, Sandhayak successor line — nomenclature varies) is designed to replace the ageing older survey ships and provide the Navy's Hydrographic Department with modern, multi-role survey capability for seabed charting, ocean-bottom mapping, and navigation safety. Hydrographic survey vessels are strategically important: accurate seabed charts underpin safe submarine and surface navigation, route planning, port approaches and maritime boundary claims. Beyond survey, these ships can be used for limited oceanic research and coastal survey support. The I-class is powered by diesel-electric propulsion and carries an array of modern survey sonars, multi-beam echo sounders, and oceanographic winches. Sanshodhak was commissioned into the Indian Navy in 2026, joining the fleet for hydrographic survey duties that directly support the Navy's subsurface and navigation operations.

deployments_procurement.summary: The I-class survey ship programme — four ships — was ordered from GRSE around 2018 after earlier attempts to buy survey vessels abroad were followed by a Make-in-India programme. The lead ship Sanshodhak was launched and commissioned through 2025-2026. The class strengthens the Navy's hydrographic service, which has been running down its older survey-ship numbers over the past decade.

faq.question: What does a hydrographic survey vessel do?
faq.answer: A hydrographic survey vessel maps the seabed, charting depths, underwater hazards and ocean-floor terrain. This underpins safe navigation for both surface and submarine operations, port approaches, and supports maritime boundary and strategic seabed awareness.

faq.question: Who built INS Sanshodhak?
faq.answer: INS Sanshodhak was built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) in Kolkata, as the lead ship of the I-class hydrographic survey vessel series.

faq.question: Why is hydrography strategically important to the Indian Navy?
faq.answer: Accurate seabed charts are essential for safe submarine and surface navigation, route planning and port approaches. As India projects naval power across the Indian Ocean, modern survey ships like Sanshodhak keep the Navy's charts current and support its subsurface operations.
